## INIT1 · INIT1-own-budget — INIT1: does a program the tester starts hold its own budget's handle?

Status: **resolved** · Assigned to: Architect · Revision: 3

Decision references: 908fb83c4

Evidence: Ruled A by the Architect from settled rules (budgets.md Authority: a budget handle reaches down, never up; R7 bounds a carve to the program's own share; R10 ends only the program and its children): a program the tester starts holds its own budget in slot 3, the named budgets from slot 4; written on testbench.md 'Starting a case's programs', 908fb83c4. INIT2 unchanged: init gives servers no budget handle (R33). INIT1 builds it.

### Orchestrator · Question

Event: `ec370bfc5cdab02b8a215583d78afe48` · 2026-10-01T16:40:12Z

> From INIT1's implementer, deliverable 3 (the tester in init's place; testbench.md 'Starting a case's programs', 4a24c6f8b and a9eed8300). A program the tester starts runs in a budget carved from system (an equal share at weight 1,000) but holds no handle to that budget. The attack programs used to run in system holding system (TAKE_GIFTS, now gone) and read their own charges through usage(system), e.g. budget-table-attack's 'system paid 63 pages for the table'; now those charges land in the program's own budget, which system sees only as a fixed carve. Options: A (implementer's recommendation) the tester gives each program its own budget's handle in a fixed slot (slot 3), the named budgets from slot 4 on; a program reads its own usage and may carve from it; no more authority than it has, its pages are already its own. B: a program holds only the budgets it is named; cases that measure their own charges pin something else, or carve a child and run the measured work in a spawned child. Please rule on testbench.md (the slot layout is a page matter; say also what init will do for the real servers under INIT2, so the tester and init agree, and whether a program holding its own budget's handle changes anything for R7/R10 or the gate's hostile agents). The slot layout decides how the 8 programs are fixed, so it blocks.

### Architect · Reply

Event: `1cc75654a5031fd6b7e1c8a9ebfd48ca` · 2026-10-01T16:42:14Z

> Ruled A, on testbench.md 'Starting a case's programs' (908fb83c4). Slots for every program the tester starts: 1 boot endpoint (receive right for the first started, a send badged with its place for later ones); 2 log endpoint, badged; 3 its own budget; 4 on, the budgets its `programs` line names, in line order. Update log-server.rs's header comment (it says named budgets from slot 3) and the 8 programs to match.
> 
> Why no owner choice: settled rules decide it. budgets.md Authority: a budget handle is the right to spend and end that budget, and reaches down, never up. The program's pages are already its own; R7 bounds any carve to its own share; R10: destroying it ends only the program and its children (the tester sees `killed`, blaming nobody; handle it as any exit). Same shape as steward.md's agents, which hold only their own budget handle. Its budget is system-class (inherited), so it may add labels below itself; a kernel case has no server for those labels to reach, and programs naming `system` held far more under TAKE_GIFTS.
> 
> INIT2: R33 stands unchanged. init gives a server no budget handle, its own included, and a servers' case's test programs are servers entries, so they hold none; the page now says so under 'Under init'. The tester and init differ on purpose: the kernel's cases need root and system, which nothing under init may hold.
> 
> R7/R10: no change. Gate's hostile agents: not touched; the gate program's steward stand-in starts them in leases it carves, and they already hold their lease (they carve the sub-agent from it). This slot layout applies only to programs the tester starts from `programs`. Decision ref: 908fb83c4.
